Sebastian's cards: five takes on C

Your pick, C (the tone-on-tone S), cleaned up five different ways, all shown with rounded corners and no red tag. Cards 1 to 3 are Spanish on the front and English on the back; cards 4 and 5 are Spanish on both sides. Handouts are off the list for now. Colours are shown as they'd come out of a print shop's toner: the blue prints noticeably duller than on a screen.

The phone number on every card is a made-up sample number. His real cell goes on only after he OKs it on Monday's paperwork.

Printing and cost (100 cards)

Before anything prints: the QR opens sanosystems.co, and the site isn't on that address yet. The print file won't build until that address opens the Spanish page, so printing waits for the switch-over. The switch-over starts with your 3-minute Cloudflare step (the token edit in the domain runbook; then tell the GM "Cloudflare done"). It has to be done by Monday for cards to be in his hands for Wednesday's doors.

FedEx can't do rounded corners same-day (online; one call to a Houston store would confirm the counter can't either). Their same-day cards (Quick Business Cards) come with square corners only. Their rounded-corner cards (Premium Business Cards) are made in about 5 business days and then shipped. FedEx lists 6 to 8 business days with overnight shipping, so ordered Monday or Tuesday they'd land around Oct 27 to 30, about a week after his first doors on Wednesday, Oct 21.

  • Why A: he has cards for the first doors, and it's under $30. Sebastian rounds them (we send the punch to him in Houston). A hand punch gives a corner a little bigger than shown here (about 4 mm) and slightly less even than a machine cut; punching 100 cards takes about 20 to 30 minutes. If the cards get used, B is the nicer reorder later: same file, thicker card, machine-cut corners.
  • Every rendition keeps its words and QR at least 1/4 inch from the edge, so either way of rounding cuts nothing off.
  • A stays well under your $100; B needs its shipping priced first. Either way we check the exact total in FedEx's cart, and their print preview, before paying.

His title (your call)

The owner reviewer said «Representante Independiente» sounds like Herbalife-style selling. All three keep "Independiente": it tells owners he's his own business, not a SANO employee, which matches his 1099 status (a card title doesn't decide that, but it shouldn't contradict it); dropping it would read warmer but blur that. Shown on card 4. On the other cards the S steps aside a little for the longer titles, so every title stays clear of it.

Same on all five

  • SANO Systems, Sebastian, his title, his cell, and on the back the QR (once the site is on sanosystems.co, it opens it in Spanish, tagged to him; every page has a language button). Every card also prints the web address.
  • Sebastian reads every Spanish line on Monday and confirms how he spells his name (Sebastian or Sebastián), and whether his cell is on WhatsApp (if yes, the card can say «Llamadas y WhatsApp» by the number, as the owner reviewer asked).
  • The owner reviewer also wished the card said in one line what SANO does. We kept it off, per your "if they have the QR code that's all it will actually need."
